landing.heroTitle: You have a career DNA that's been quietly
landing.heroDesc: You've probably never noticed it, but it's been there all along. 5 minutes to decode it.
landing.scrollHint: Your career DNA might surprise you
landing.card1Desc: Your career identity — revealed instantly. Archetype, personality dimensions, cognitive style, shadow side. A mirror built from 5 psychology frameworks, not a label from a quiz.
landing.card2Desc: AI-generated career report: top matches, career anchors, growth paths, and blind spots. Cross-analyzed from your unique response pattern — not generic career advice.
landing.card3Desc: A coach who has read your entire assessment — values, tensions, career directions. Plus AI-powered action tools: resume optimizer, interview prep, elevator pitch, and more.
landing.archetypeDesc: Each archetype maps two interest dimensions to a career identity — with its own strengths, growth edges, and career directions. You'll see which roles naturally fit, which ones drain you, and why your past choices make more sense than you thought.
landing.abyssTitle:
What you share here
never leaves the deep.
landing.abyssDesc: Real self-exploration requires real privacy. Your doubts, ambitions, and contradictions — protected here, and always yours to export or delete. That's the point.
landing.bottomTitle:
Ready to hear what your
career instinct has been saying?
landing.bottomDesc: The pattern behind your career decisions has been there all along. It just needs a name.
landing.bottomNote: Start free · 5 minutes · Discover your archetype across 5 psychology frameworks
landing.mockArchetypeTagline: Seeing what others miss and mending what matters
landing.breathQuote:
The career that fits you isn't something you find.
It's something you recognize.
landing.clarityStep1Desc: 38 interest and values questions, 5 minutes. Discover which of 12 career archetypes fits your natural pattern.
landing.clarityStep2Desc: 86 scenario-based questions across personality, values, and cognitive style. Not checkboxes — real dilemmas that reveal what your résumé never shows.
landing.clarityStep3Desc: Your psychological profile — revealed instantly. Career archetype, personality dimensions, cognitive style, shadow side. A mirror that shows who you really are, not who your résumé says you are.
landing.clarityStep4Desc: AI-generated career report with personalized matches, growth paths, and an AI coach who knows your full profile. Not generic advice — a map drawn from your unique pattern.
landing.clarityTime: Quick Dive: ~5 min · Deep Dive: ~20 min
landing.quickDiveCardDesc: 5 min · 38 quick questions · instant interest profile
landing.narrativeExploreCardDesc: 15-20 min · 38 immersive camp scenarios · story-driven discovery
landing.deepDiveCardDesc: ~20 min · 86 questions across 3 modules · Full career report + AI coaching
landing.resonanceTitle:
Look up at the stars. Feel the ground beneath your feet.
Your path lives somewhere between the dream and the real.
landing.resonanceDesc: Deep Dive was built for people navigating between worlds — between cultures, between careers, between who they are and who they're becoming.
landing.forWhoTitle:
Built for those navigating
uncharted waters
landing.forWhoSubtitle: Whether you're crossing borders, changing paths, or outrunning a wave of change — Deep Dive meets you where you are.
landing.forWho1Desc: Building a career across countries and cultures without a home-court advantage. Deep Dive maps how your cross-cultural identity shapes your career strengths — so you stop seeing it as a gap and start using it as an edge.
landing.forWho2Desc: Your industry is shifting and standing still isn't an option. Deep Dive reveals which of your core patterns are future-proof — so you know whether to double down, pivot, or reinvent.
landing.forWho3Desc: Feeling the pull toward something new but unsure which direction fits the real you. Deep Dive identifies the thread connecting your past roles — and points to where it leads next.
landing.forWho4Desc: Infinite options, zero clarity. Deep Dive cuts through the noise with a profile built on how you actually think and decide — not what the market says you should want.
landing.trustFrameworks: Built on O*NET Interest Profiler · IPIP · Schwartz Values · Big Five
landing._socialProofQuotesRemoved: Placeholder testimonials removed — will add real user quotes when available

quickDive.missionR: You were the first to walk into the generator shed, tools in hand, pulling open the panel to find the cause. During repairs you took on the hardest part by hand. For you, doing and understanding have never been separate things.
quickDive.missionI: You spent the longest time in the archive room, connecting decades of records into a single thread. Analyzing the stream samples, you wrote out your full reasoning. Understanding alone isn't enough — you need it to become something tangible.
quickDive.missionA: Designing the last evening's event, you considered space and flow for every segment. Your personal presentation used a form no one expected. Your imagination isn't idle dreaming — it carries the execution to make ideas real.
quickDive.missionS: On the mountain trail at night, you sat with Kai, saying nothing, just being there. On the fourth day, you walked over to Nora. You help through action, not words. Your care isn't comforting phrases; it's problem-solving hands.
quickDive.missionE: Planning the last 36 hours, you stood up and drew the action chart. Negotiating with the village, you laid out the terms clearly. Your leadership isn't verbal — it's imprinted on everything you've done.
quickDive.missionC: You completed Ruth's safety checklist item by item. Analyzing five days of data, you found three improvable patterns. Archiving records, every document was dated and categorized. You pursue the perfect balance between efficiency and quality.

This kind of pattern often generates the sharpest career insights in the final report. 72 items to go — too early to draw conclusions just yet.
microFeedback.ipipPatternContrastNormalInsight: After 48 items, "{{high}}" is your strongest emerging signal, while "{{low}}" is most restrained. 72 items remain — this contrast may deepen, or it may surprise you.

microFeedback.ipipOutlineNEContrastInsight: An interesting combination appeared: rich inner emotional world, but {{level}} outward social energy. This combination will get a unique interpretation in your final report. Two chapters to go.

microFeedback.bonusContrastInsight: A notable contrast appeared between your inner emotional world and outward social energy — this combination often maps to specific career strengths. What exactly? You'll see in the report.

reportPanels.careerTensionsDesc: These tensions are not flaws — they are dimensions to manage in your career choices.
reportPanels.consistencyTeamRole: Your natural preference in a team and the leadership style you actually choose show some tension — this may mean you reveal different sides of yourself in different contexts.
reportPanels.consistencyRiskTolerance: Your attitudes toward stability and freedom sent different signals across questions — this may reflect a genuine inner negotiation between risk and security.
reportPanels.consistencyEnergyCoherence: There's a contradiction between what energizes you and what drains you — it's worth exploring the subtle differences in how you manage energy across contexts.
reportPanels.consistencyValueCoherence: Your instincts in value trade-off dilemmas and your final value priority ranking diverge somewhat — this may reflect a tension between ideals and reality.
reportPanels.consistencySocialTension: You gave different answers for what you 'should do' versus what you 'would do' in a social scenario — this tension reflects a gap between your social cognition and natural inclination.
reportPanels.consistencyDecisionTension: Your ideal approach and actual behavior in team decisions differ — this may be a signal that you're balancing efficiency against relationships.
reportPanels.consistencyResponsibilityTension: Your philosophy on communication responsibility and your actual behavior don't fully align — this kind of gap is common across different cultures and organizations.
